questions.text: Which tools traditionally form the basis of building PostgreSQL from source?
questions.explanation: The traditional way to build PostgreSQL from source is based on GNU Make and Autoconf.

questions.text: Starting with which PostgreSQL version can Meson be used for building?
questions.explanation: The course material states that the Meson build system can be used starting with PostgreSQL 16.

questions.text: Which capabilities does the readline library provide?
questions.explanation: readline provides command-line editing, command history, and completion.

questions.text: Which build tool does Meson use by default to compile PostgreSQL?
questions.explanation: Meson uses Ninja by default. After configuring the build directory, compilation is performed with the ninja command.

source.locator: Short Version: meson setup, ninja, ninja install

questions.text: Which commands are part of the short traditional PostgreSQL build and installation sequence using Autoconf and Make?
questions.explanation: The short traditional build procedure consists of configuration with ./configure, compilation with make, and installation with make install.

source.section: Building and Installing with Autoconf and Make

questions.text: What is the initdb utility used for?

answers.text: Creating a new PostgreSQL database cluster

questions.explanation: initdb creates a new PostgreSQL database cluster.

source.locator: Creating a New PostgreSQL Database Cluster

questions.text: Which statements about the user who runs initdb are true?

answers.text: initdb should be run as the user under which the PostgreSQL server will run
The user needs full access to the cluster files and directories being created
The PostgreSQL server must not run as the operating-system superuser
initdb must be run as root

questions.explanation: initdb must be run as the owner of the future server process; running it as the operating-system superuser is not allowed.

source.locator: User Running initdb and the PostgreSQL Server

questions.text: How can the cluster data directory be specified to initdb?
questions.explanation: The data directory is specified with -D/--pgdata or the PGDATA environment variable.

questions.text: Which locale provider does initdb use by default?

answers.text: PostgreSQL does not use a locale provider

questions.explanation: By default, initdb uses the libc locale provider.

source.locator: libc Provider Is Used by Default

questions.text: Which statements about initdb -k/--data-checksums are true?

answers.text: Checksums are calculated for all objects in all databases in the cluster
Checksum errors are reflected in pg_stat_database
Checksums apply only to system catalogs

questions.explanation: -k/--data-checksums enables data-page checksums; when enabled, they apply to all objects in all databases in the cluster.

questions.text: Which statements about initdb --no-sync are true?

answers.text: After an unexpected operating-system failure, the data directory can become corrupted
The option can be useful for testing
The option is recommended for production

questions.explanation: --no-sync disables waiting for files to be safely written to disk. This can make initdb faster, but it increases the risk of data corruption after a failure and is not recommended for production.

questions.text: What does the initdb -U/--username option set?

answers.text: The name of the initial PostgreSQL superuser

questions.explanation: -U/--username sets the name of the initial superuser; by default, the name of the operating-system user running initdb is used.

questions.text: What is initdb -X/--waldir used for?

answers.text: Specifying the directory where WAL is stored
Specifying the directory for logical backups

questions.explanation: -X/--waldir sets the directory where the write-ahead log (WAL) will be stored.

questions.text: Which operations does pg_ctl support?

answers.text: Automatically running VACUUM on all databases

questions.explanation: pg_ctl is used to initialize and manage the server: start, stop, restart, reload, status, promote, and other operations.

questions.text: Which shutdown modes does pg_ctl stop support?
questions.explanation: pg_ctl stop supports smart, fast, and immediate modes.

questions.text: Which pg_ctl shutdown mode is used by default?

answers.text: A mode must always be specified explicitly

questions.explanation: If -m is not specified, pg_ctl uses fast mode.

questions.text: What happens during PostgreSQL shutdown in smart mode?

answers.text: The server waits for existing clients to disconnect
All server processes are terminated immediately

questions.explanation: Smart shutdown rejects new connections and waits for existing clients to disconnect.

questions.text: Which statements about pg_ctl stop -m immediate are true?

answers.text: The normal clean-shutdown procedure is not performed
Crash recovery will be required at the next startup
The server waits for all user sessions to finish

questions.explanation: Immediate shutdown terminates server processes immediately without a clean shutdown, so crash recovery will be required at the next startup.

questions.text: What does pg_ctl reload do?

answers.text: Sends SIGHUP to the postgres process so configuration is reread
Completely stops and restarts the server

questions.explanation: reload sends SIGHUP to the server, after which PostgreSQL rereads postgresql.conf, pg_hba.conf, and other configuration files.

questions.text: What does pg_ctl status show when the server is running?

answers.text: The server PID and startup command-line options
A list of all tables in the cluster

questions.explanation: For a running server, pg_ctl status displays the PID and command-line options used to start it.

questions.text: What state must the server be in before running pg_checksums?

answers.text: The server must be shut down cleanly
The server must run in read-only mode
The server must be in recovery mode
The server state does not matter

questions.explanation: Before running pg_checksums, the PostgreSQL server must be shut down cleanly.

source.locator: The Server Must Be Stopped Before Running pg_checksums

questions.text: Which main operations does pg_checksums support?
questions.explanation: pg_checksums can check, enable, or disable data checksums for a cluster.

questions.text: Which statements about pg_checksums --no-sync are true?

answers.text: If the operating system fails, the directory containing modified files can be corrupted
The option is not recommended for production
In --check mode the option speeds up checksum verification

questions.explanation: --no-sync disables waiting for files to be safely written. It is mainly useful for testing and has no effect in --check mode.

questions.text: What happens to cluster files when checksums are enabled and disabled with pg_checksums?

answers.text: When enabling, checksums are calculated for relation-file blocks
When enabling, relation blocks are rewritten in place
When disabling, only pg_control is changed
When disabling, all relation files are completely rewritten

questions.explanation: When enabling checksums, pg_checksums calculates a checksum for each relation block and rewrites the blocks; when disabling checksums, only pg_control is changed.

source.locator: File Changes during enable and disable

questions.text: What is a PostgreSQL database cluster?

answers.text: A set of server configuration files
The set of databases served simultaneously by one PostgreSQL instance

questions.explanation: A single PostgreSQL instance works with multiple databases at the same time; this set of databases is called a database cluster.

questions.text: What is a PostgreSQL server (server instance)?

answers.text: The program that manages a database cluster

questions.explanation: The cluster is the data stored in files, while the server or server instance is the program that manages that cluster.

questions.text: When is installing PostgreSQL from source useful?

answers.text: When only standard build options must be used
When nonstandard build options are needed
When a build for a specific architecture is required
When you need to understand how the PostgreSQL build process works

questions.explanation: The material emphasizes the value of understanding source builds for nonstandard options, specific architectures, and a general understanding of the installation process.

questions.text: How does obtaining source from the git repository differ from using a source archive?

answers.text: Git can build a version at a specific commit, including the latest development state
Building from git normally requires a broader set of tools
The archive already contains some generated C files
An archive can build only PostgreSQL 16, while git can build only PostgreSQL 17

questions.explanation: Git gives access to any commit but requires additional tools; release archives already contain some generated files.

questions.text: Which software is required for a traditional PostgreSQL build from source?
questions.explanation: The required software listed in the material includes tar, gzip/bzip2, GNU make, and a C compiler.

questions.text: What are the zlib, lz4, and zstd libraries used for when building PostgreSQL?
questions.explanation: The material explicitly states that zlib, lz4, and zstd are used for compression.

questions.text: When might the readline library be unnecessary in a PostgreSQL server installation?

answers.text: If psql will not be run interactively in a terminal
If the server listens on TCP/IP

questions.explanation: Readline is primarily needed for a convenient interactive command line; the material notes that it may be unnecessary if psql is not used interactively in a terminal.

questions.text: Which languages may be needed as additional dependencies for PostgreSQL procedural languages?
questions.explanation: The material lists Perl, Python, and Tcl for using PL/Perl, PL/Python, and PL/Tcl.

questions.text: Which components can be used for authentication and encryption when building PostgreSQL?
questions.explanation: In the optional software section, the material associates Kerberos, OpenSSL, OpenLDAP, and PAM with authentication and encryption.

questions.text: What can the ICU library be used for when building PostgreSQL?
questions.explanation: ICU is listed as a library for cross-platform Unicode support.

questions.text: What is true about make check when building PostgreSQL with Autoconf/Make?

answers.text: It should be run only after make install
It runs regression tests on the built server before installation
It should be run as a regular user, not root
It can be repeated later for another check

questions.explanation: The documentation recommends make check after building and before installation; tests are run as a regular user, not root.

questions.text: How does make world-bin differ from make world?

answers.text: world-bin builds only the server without utilities
world-bin builds documentation while world does not
world-bin includes contrib but not documentation; world includes both contrib and documentation

questions.explanation: make world includes additional modules and documentation, while make world-bin includes additional modules without documentation.

source.locator: make world and make world-bin Targets

questions.text: Which configure option is normally used to change the PostgreSQL installation root directory?
questions.explanation: The --prefix option sets the installation tree prefix instead of the default /usr/local/pgsql.

questions.text: Which configure options enable the corresponding optional PostgreSQL features?
questions.explanation: The documentation describes --with-python, --with-lz4, and --with-zstd as options that enable the corresponding capabilities.

questions.text: What is the consequence of building with --without-readline?

answers.text: Command-line editing and history are disabled in psql

questions.explanation: --without-readline disables Readline/libedit, so psql loses command-line editing and history.

questions.text: What does meson setup build do during the PostgreSQL build process?

answers.text: Creates and configures the build directory named build
Removes the results of a previous installation

questions.explanation: meson setup creates and configures the build directory; the builddir argument is mandatory for this command.

questions.text: Which Meson command changes settings of an already-created build directory?
questions.explanation: After the initial meson setup, build-directory settings are changed with meson configure.

questions.text: What is true about meson test when building PostgreSQL?

answers.text: It is intended only to delete the build directory
It runs regression tests on the built server
It should be run as a regular user, not root
It can be run before PostgreSQL is installed

questions.explanation: The documentation recommends meson test for regression testing after building and before installation, as a regular user.

questions.text: Which commands correctly belong to the Meson/Ninja PostgreSQL build lifecycle?

answers.text: ninja initdb — initialize the build directory
ninja install — install the built files

questions.explanation: The documentation describes ninja install, ninja clean, and ninja uninstall for installation, cleanup, and removal of the installed files.

source.locator: ninja install, ninja uninstall, ninja clean

questions.text: What does the initdb --pwfile option do?

answers.text: Reads the initial superuser password from the first line of the specified file
Writes the superuser password to postgresql.conf

questions.explanation: --pwfile makes initdb read the initial superuser password from the first line of the specified file.

questions.text: What is initdb --sync-only intended for?

answers.text: Safely synchronizing database files to disk without performing the other initdb operations

questions.explanation: --sync-only synchronizes database files to disk and exits without performing the other initdb operations.

questions.text: Which statements about initdb --wal-segsize are true?

answers.text: The default WAL segment size is 16 MB
The value is specified in megabytes and must be a power of two within the allowed range
The size can be freely changed after cluster initialization
This parameter is set when the cluster is initialized

questions.explanation: The WAL segment size is set at initdb time; the default is 16 MB, and it cannot later be changed with this option.

questions.text: What does pg_ctl restart actually do?

answers.text: Stops the server and then starts it again

questions.explanation: restart is a stop followed by a start and can be used for changes that require a full server restart.

questions.text: What is pg_ctl promote used for?

answers.text: Taking a standby server out of standby mode and switching it to read/write operation
Promoting an ordinary user to superuser

questions.explanation: promote takes a server out of standby mode and switches it to normal read/write operation.

questions.text: What task does the -l option solve with pg_ctl start?

answers.text: Specifies a file for server output

questions.explanation: When starting the server, the -l option to pg_ctl directs server output to the specified log file.

questions.text: Why can startup and maintenance commands for a packaged PostgreSQL installation differ from commands for a 'clean' PostgreSQL source build?

answers.text: Because packaged PostgreSQL does not use operating-system processes
Because the package vendor can integrate installation and startup with the system's standard tools
Because pg_ctl exists only in the source version
Because the packaged version has no data directory

questions.explanation: The runtime chapter notes that packaged products are usually integrated by the vendor with the system's installation and startup mechanisms, so details may differ from a 'clean' source build.

source.locator: Assumptions about “Clean” PostgreSQL and Packaged Products

questions.text: Why is installing PostgreSQL from prebuilt packages usually preferable to building from source?

answers.text: Such installation is clearer and supported by system tools
It is usually easier to update
It always contains the newest development branch from git
The PGDG repository can be used for current versions

questions.explanation: The material describes package installation as clear, supported, and easy to update; the PGDG repository is mentioned for obtaining a current version.

questions.text: What is true about pg_createcluster on Ubuntu?

answers.text: It is a wrapper around initdb
Package installation creates a cluster named main
Checksums are enabled by default during this initialization
Package installation configures automatic server startup/shutdown together with the operating system

questions.explanation: On Ubuntu, pg_createcluster wraps initdb; the package creates a cluster named main, checksums are disabled by default, and server startup/shutdown is integrated with the operating system.

questions.text: Which statements about pg_dropcluster and pg_createcluster are true?

answers.text: pg_dropcluster is used to remove a cluster
Both utilities are Ubuntu-specific in the context of the material
On other systems, a cluster can be initialized explicitly with initdb

questions.explanation: The material identifies pg_createcluster and pg_dropcluster as Ubuntu-specific; on other systems initdb and appropriate operating-system tools are used.

questions.text: How should a PostgreSQL instance from Ubuntu packages be managed instead of invoking pg_ctl directly?

answers.text: Only through the pg_ctl() SQL function

questions.explanation: In the Ubuntu package distribution, pg_ctlcluster is used as a wrapper around pg_ctl; on other systems pg_ctl can be used directly.

questions.text: Which differences are typical between PostgreSQL in a virtual machine and managed PostgreSQL?

answers.text: A virtual environment has virtualization overhead
In a virtual machine, the administrator can have full access to the instance
In a managed service, the provider handles much of the administration
A managed service always provides full access to the instance and operating system

questions.explanation: The material compares virtualization overhead and full administrative access in a VM with restricted access and greater provider responsibility in DBaaS.

questions.text: What is the correct sequence for enabling checksums in an existing PostgreSQL cluster with pg_checksums?

answers.text: Enable checksums → stop the server → check → start
Stop the server → check checksum state → enable checksums → start the server
Start the server → enable checksums → stop → check
Check checksums on a running server → enable → restart

questions.explanation: The practice specifies this order: stop the server, check the checksum state, enable checksums, and then start the server.

questions.text: What is true about pg_checksums --check mode?

answers.text: It is the default mode if no other mode is specified
If no errors are found, the command returns a zero exit status
If at least one error is found, a nonzero status is returned
This mode automatically repairs damaged pages

questions.explanation: --check is the default mode; the exit status indicates whether checksum errors were found.

questions.text: Which precautions are important when enabling or disabling checksums in a large or replicated cluster?

answers.text: Until the operation finishes, do not start the server or other programs that write to the data directory
With block-level file copying, checksum mode must be changed consistently across nodes
A safe option is to recreate standby servers after the operation on the primary
For speed, it is recommended to run the server in parallel and write to the cluster

questions.explanation: The documentation warns about long-running operations and the risks of concurrent writes; with block-level replication, checksum mode must be consistent across nodes.

questions.text: What happens to the checksum configuration if pg_checksums is interrupted during enable or disable?

answers.text: It is necessarily switched partially to the new state
The checksum configuration remains unchanged, and the operation can be run again
PostgreSQL permanently prevents pg_checksums from being run again

questions.explanation: If pg_checksums is interrupted during enable or disable, the checksum configuration state remains unchanged and the operation can be repeated.
